parts.visual:
A customer's software crashes. They call the company angry. The agent fixes the bug. This is Customer Support.
A month later, an agent notices the customer isn't using the new 'Reporting' feature. The agent calls the customer, trains them on the feature, and helps them generate more revenue. This is Customer Success.

The Distinction:
1. Customer Support: Reactive. They solve problems when things break. Their goal is to close the ticket as fast as possible.
2. Customer Success: Proactive. They ensure the customer is achieving their business goals using the software. Their goal is to drive retention and expansion.
parts.audio: Customer Support is a cost center; they put out fires. Customer Success is a revenue generator; they build relationships that lead to massive contract renewals and upsells.

questions.question: A Customer Success Manager (CSM) sees on the dashboard that a massive enterprise client hasn't logged into the software in 14 days. What should the CSM do?
options: Proactively call the client immediately. A drop in usage is the number one early warning sign of churn. The CSM must intervene, find out why they aren't using it, and fix the adoption problem before the renewal date.
questions.correct_answer: Proactively call the client immediately. A drop in usage is the number one early warning sign of churn. The CSM must intervene, find out why they aren't using it, and fix the adoption problem before the renewal date.
questions.explanation: If you wait until they ask to cancel, you have already lost.

questions.question: Listen to the CSM negotiating with a client. What is their primary goal during this 'QBR' (Quarterly Business Review)?
questions.tts_text: Here is the data from the last three months. Our software saved your team 400 hours of labor, which equates to $20,000 in ROI. Based on this success, we recommend upgrading to the Enterprise tier next quarter.
options: Proving ROI and Upselling. The CSM uses the QBR to formally remind the executives exactly how much value the software provided, cementing the relationship and setting the stage for an upgrade.
questions.correct_answer: Proving ROI and Upselling. The CSM uses the QBR to formally remind the executives exactly how much value the software provided, cementing the relationship and setting the stage for an upgrade.
questions.explanation: Never assume the client remembers how much money you saved them.

questions.question: Why do elite SaaS companies separate 'Sales' and 'Customer Success' into two different departments?
options: Because the skillsets are opposite. Sales is the aggressive hunter who closes the deal and moves on. Customer Success is the empathetic farmer who nurtures the relationship for the next 5 years.
questions.correct_answer: Because the skillsets are opposite. Sales is the aggressive hunter who closes the deal and moves on. Customer Success is the empathetic farmer who nurtures the relationship for the next 5 years.
questions.explanation: Hunters and farmers have entirely different psychologies.

questions.question: What happens if a startup only invests in Customer Support and completely ignores Customer Success?
options: They save a lot of money.

They will suffer massive 'Silent Churn'. Customers won't call support because nothing is technically 'broken'. But because no one is proactively teaching them how to get value, they will quietly cancel their contracts.
questions.correct_answer: They will suffer massive 'Silent Churn'. Customers won't call support because nothing is technically 'broken'. But because no one is proactively teaching them how to get value, they will quietly cancel their contracts.
questions.explanation: Absence of complaints does not equal satisfaction.

questions.explanation: They don't fix bugs; they fix business outcomes.
